thread.title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stocks Drop As Tech Pullback, Nissan CEO's Arrest Take Toll

author: morningstar.com
title: ASIA MARKETS: Asian Stocks Drop As Tech Pullback, Nissan CEO's Arrest Take Toll
text:
By Dow Jones Newswires
Auto, electronics sectors weigh on Nikkei; tech stocks sink Hang Seng
Asian stock markets fell Tuesday, following tech-led declines on Wall Street.
Japan's Nikkei was down nearly 1.1%, with electronics and machinery stocks among the biggest decliners. Sony (6758.TO) was down 3% while Fanuc (6954.TO) and Hitachi (6501.TO) both dropped.
But Japan's auto sector was the most watched following the arrest of Nissan CEO Carlos Ghosn on Monday. Alliance partners Nissan (NSANY) and Mitsubishi (7211.TO) slid in early trading, with Nissan at almost 2 1/2 -year lows, ending down 5.5%. Rival Toyota (7203.TO) benefited, climbing 1.6%.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 2%, with Tencent (0700.HK) down 3% and smartphone-component firms AAC (2018.HK) and Sunny Optical (2382.HK) also falling. Xiaomi (1810.HK) jumped 8% after its third-quarter earnings report.
In mainland China, the Shanghai Composite was down 2.1% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite dropped 2.7%. Among large caps, real estate was off some 1% after Monday's sharp bounce. Financials, which also were strong Monday, pulled back.
A report about another round of production cuts for iPhones (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shares-of-apple-iphone-suppliers-extend-losses-after-wsj-report-of-further-production-cuts-2018-11-19)weighed on Apple (AAPL) suppliers in Asia. Taiwan's Taiex fell 0.8% as product assembler Hon Hai (2317.TW) dropped 3.2% to hit fresh five-year lows and Taiwan Semiconductor (2330.TW) declined 1.8%. Korean memory-chip maker SK Hynix (000660.SE) slid another 3.3% and Samsung Electronics (005930.SE) lost 2% as the Kospi dropped 0.8%.
Australia's benchmark index was down 0.3%, and New Zealand and Singapore posted losses as well.
